audit.whatIsWrong: Two-layer chart disagreement at the last two rows. Full phases[5].side said 'Akshan' and phases[6].side said 'Skill'; content win[5] and win[6] both said 'Aurelion Sol'.
audit.why: The packet levelChart gives Aurelion Sol both stages, and both full whys already describe him winning them ('your E executes the back line of every wave', 'You are the scaling endgame'). The sides were the stale half.
audit.corrected: phases[5].side and phases[6].side both move to 'Aurelion Sol' so the row and the sentence under it agree. Rows 0-4 left alone — packet, content and prose all already say Akshan.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid-game spike was described as an ally revive on Comeuppance. Comeuppance does not revive anyone — it is a lock-on that stores bullets and deals damage based on missing health at 2500 range, 100/85/70s. The resurrect is on Going Rogue (W): killing a Scoundrel resurrects the allies that Scoundrel killed.
audit.why: The revive is attached to the wrong slot in whys[4], spikes[1], content mid and wants.foe[2]. A player told to 'zone the ult range' to stop a revive is being taught the wrong counterplay entirely — the revive is gated on him killing a marked champion, not on his ultimate.
audit.corrected: All four rewritten around what Comeuppance actually is: a missing-health finisher from 2500 out, which is why entering any trade already chipped is the real error.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Comeuppance stops on the FIRST champion, minion or structure hit.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'dealing damage based on missing health to the first champion, minion, or structure hit'. Keeping a single minion on the line between you and Akshan removes the entire ultimate — and Aurelion Sol farms from behind his wave anyway, so it costs him nothing to do.

audit.whatIsWrong: Heroic Swing's terrain requirement was never mentioned; the page treated it as a free engage on an 18s cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's E text: 'fires a grappling hook into terrain then swings around it... gets knocked off when colliding with champions or terrain'. In open mid lane he has nothing to hook, and a champion collision — including a stunned body — drops him off the rope mid-swing.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[1].d and tradeBad.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dirty Fighting's shield was absent. Every third hit from his attacks and abilities shields him when the target is a champion.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol's damage is a slow burn, so a shield that regenerates every three hits eats exactly the trade pattern the page recommends. It is the reason chip-trading him does not work pre-item.
audit.corrected: Added to dontsFull[0].d, tradeBad and content early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The trading advice never used the range numbers that decide it.
audit.why: Avengerang is 850 and extends its range on every enemy it hits; Breath of Light is 750. He out-ranges the beam before the wave is even involved, and more so through it.
audit.corrected: Named in breakdown.early, spikes[0] and content early.

audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, Astral Flight 22s at rank 1, and Going Rogue drops from 18s to 2s by rank 5 — that last number is the one that changes how you ward the lane late.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the Heroic Swing and Astral Flight numbers plus the terrain requirement.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] ended 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain.' Akshan has no heal in his kit — Dirty Fighting grants a shield.
audit.why: Grievous Wounds does not touch a shield, so the line sends the player's gold to a dead stat.
audit.corrected: Replaced with an explicit 'he shields, not heals' instruction.
sources: enemyKit P text — shield flag, no heal flag on any slot

edits.before: Akshan's Avengerang ricochets through the minion wave for free poke damage while he stays out of your Q's effective range, and Going Rogue stealth near cover lets him reposition for follow-up autos you never see coming. You lack the early burst to punish his hit-and-fade pattern, so every trade favors him unless he overextends into your zone. Stand behind your wave, don't feed him free ricochet angles, and save your stars rather than forcing bad trades.

notes: Biggest find: the revive was attached to the wrong ability in four places. Comeuppance (R) is a lock-on missing-health finisher; the resurrect belongs to Going Rogue (W) and only fires when Akshan kills a champion marked as a Scoundrel. Anyone playing to 'zone the ult range to stop the revive' is playing a mechanic that does not exist. Second: Comeuppance stops on the first champion, minion or structure hit, which is the single most useful thing an Aurelion Sol can know here and was nowhere on the page. Data note repeated from the akali file: the ownerKit 'terrain: creates terrain' flag on Astral Flight contradicts Riot's description (it flies OVER terrain) — I never wrote a terrain-creation claim. Akshan's own W also carries that flag and Riot's W text is camouflage, not terrain, so that flag is misfiring on him too; I described Going Rogue as camouflage per the description. MIRROR: the brief reported mirrorAlreadyAudited=false and mirrorFindings=null, but audits/mid/akshan_mid__aurelionsol.json already exists on disk — the brief's mirror lookup appears stale. My chart edits only align the full layer to the packet and the content layer, which is the same direction any mirror pass would take, but the user may want mirror-fix.js run over this pair. Unverified and left alone: whether Falling Star's stun specifically knocks Akshan off Heroic Swing mid-swing (Riot says champion collision knocks him off; I worded dosFull[1] to Riot's wording rather than claiming the stun does it), and tenacity/QSS behaviour on Falling Star.
